findings: §5.1 miscount/jam recovery breaks the stated invariant: 'The bar therefore ends 2, 4, or 6 clicks lower than it started' — but the recovery rule says a mid-Set miscount/jam keeps whatever partial down-clicks already happened and then runs a fresh full eight-click Set on top, so a single round's net drop can exceed 6 clicks. The text never reconciles this with the 'always 2, 4, or 6' claim used elsewhere (e.g. the endgame countdown math in §6).

§6 arithmetic is internally inconsistent: for the largest drop pattern (down 7 then up 1, net -6/round, down-phase max 7), simulating from the 33.0mm start (31 clicks to the 17.5mm stop) hits the bottom stop mid-down-phase in round 5 (24 clicks after 4 rounds + 7th down-click = 31), not the stated 'at the largest, 6' rounds.

§5.7 Salvage is gated on 'the game is not over,' but Salvage is itself a sub-step of The Take (§4 step 5), and per §6 the game 'ends at the end of the round in which the setter says Bottom' — i.e. the Bottom round's own Take is still part of that final round. It's ambiguous whether Salvage is allowed during the Bottom round's Take (self-referential: is the game 'over' before its own last Take completes?), and this matters because Salvage moves a block from score line to rail, which changes the §7 tiebreak #2 ('more blocks remaining in the rail').
